reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it discusses cryptocurrency and presents market-cap information, while mentioning OneCoin as a newly emerging company. The title and signup link suggest promotion, but the recorded speech does not state a concrete return promise or explain a required payment or data request, so the video does not establish a deceptive solicitation.

opening.argument: Judge, read the forecast alongside the destination supplied to viewers. The speaker says OneCoin will “start to gain momentum extremely quickly,” and the description provides a OneCoin signup address and Skype contact. The speech does not explicitly promise a return, but the combination invites viewers to register while the company is presented as an opportunity gaining speed. That is more than detached market commentary.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense is right that no return figure or required payment is stated. But those omissions do not make the signup destination irrelevant. The speaker's disclaimer about giving a company presentation does not resolve why the description supplies a way to register with the company he predicts will gain momentum.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: “Gain momentum” describes the company, not an expected token price or viewer return. A signup address permits an inference of promotion, but the supplied speech does not ask viewers to buy a token or say registration will yield gains. The cited market discussion remains about cryptocurrencies generally.

opening.argument: Judge, the financial pitch is not confined to the narration. The displayed market page repeatedly carries a banner offering to “Start Mining Bitcoin” and “Get started now for only $9.95,” with a “Learn More” button. That pairs access to mining with a stated price and an action, directly above cryptocurrency market figures. Alongside the speaker's emphasis on crypto as a trend, it gives viewers a paid participation prompt within the material they are watching, even though the speaker does not voice the banner's offer.

citations.quote: Guys, this is definitely a trend.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense focuses on the absence of a spoken return promise, but the visible banner supplies a price and action that its account leaves out. Market-cap figures and Bitcoin infrastructure may be the speaker's topic; they do not erase the paid mining invitation displayed above the figures.

citations.quote: Bitcoin is currently in a leading position, its капитализация is more than 6 billion.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The banner appears on the market-information page, not as a demonstrated offer by the speaker or OneCoin. It advertises starting mining for a price, but the supplied material does not establish recurring income, a promised return, or any viewer following that ad. The narration identifies the page as a place to inspect currencies.

opening.argument: Judge, the educational framing also serves a promotional sequence. The speaker introduces OneCoin as a company viewers likely have not heard of, predicts that it will gain momentum quickly, then discusses established cryptocurrencies and their market positions. The title names OneCoin, while the description supplies its signup address. The market lesson can therefore lend credibility to the named company and steer interested viewers toward registration, even without an explicit instruction to invest.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this market analysis overlooks the placement of the company's name and signup destination around that analysis. The speaker's denial that he is presenting the company limits what he claims to be doing; it does not negate the promotional effect of pairing a favorable forecast with a registration route. The defense's lack-of-payment point narrows the evidence, but does not make the registration route disappear.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A promotional reading is possible, but promotion alone does not establish a deceptive token-return scheme. The forecast concerns a company's momentum; the supplied speech does not connect signup to a token purchase, appreciation, or dividends. The speaker spends the cited passage identifying other cryptocurrencies and their relative capitalization, which supports the defense's reading of the recorded content as market discussion.
